articleTitle: Dimensioning of Zero Grid Electricity Cellular Networking with Solar Powered Off-Grid BS
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The continuous deployment of cellular base stations (BSs) is forcing the energy consumption in a wireless network at a staggering rate. This remarkable rise in energy utilization has become increasingly important for the mobile operators due to the significant economic and environmental aspect. The unavailability of reliable electricity grids push the telecom operators to install diesel generators (DG), which not only increases operational expenditure but also contributes to the considerable amount of carbon footprints. This paper aims to address sustainability of renewable power resources and ecological issues for off-grid cellular BSs. We consider all the macro BSs in Long Term Evolution (LTE) cellular network are solely driven by the renewable energy source such as solar energy and equipped with sufficient energy storage devices along with energy management units (EMU). In particular, we analyze the dimensioning of stand-alone capacity of on-site PV panel, power electronic converter and batteries based on the daily energy need of the BS. Three key considerations have been discussed throughout the study using HOMER optimization tool: optimal solar architecture, energy yield analysis and the cost analysis. Simulation results show that the proposed solution ensures 100% energy autonomy and long-term energy balance for the LTE macro BS.

articleTitle: Performance of SVM, CNN, and ANN with BoW, HOG, and Image Pixels in Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this study, we present the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolution Neural Network (CNN), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with Bag of Words (BoW), Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), and Image Pixels (IP) for face recognition. SVM, CNN, and ANN are machine learning approaches and has been used for pattern recognition, especially in face recognition technology. BoW, HOG, and IP are being used for image feature extraction. The testing has been conducted from publicly available AT&T face database. Every individual subject consists of 10 images with different facial expression, different illumination and the dimensions of the images is unified as 92-by-112 pixels with PGM formats. SVM achieved recognition accuracy of 97.00%, 96.00%, and 98.00% with subsequently BoW, HOG, and IP. CNN achieved recognition accuracy of 94.00%, 99.00%, and 99.50% with subsequently BoW, HOG, and IP. ANN achieved recognition accuracy of 96.00%, 99.00%, and 99.50% with subsequently BoW, HOG, and IP. The experimental results show that the IP with ANN approach clearly outperformed the others approaches.

articleTitle: Predict Student's Academic Performance and Evaluate the Impact of Different Attributes on the Performance Using Data Mining Techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In Educational Data Mining, many data mining techniques are applied to extract hidden knowledge from student data. This knowledge helps educational institutes to improve their teaching quality. Different attributes have an impact on student's academic performance. Behavioral and student absent in class has an effect on their academic performance. In this paper, the effect of above two categories of features will be measured using some data mining techniques. For classification Naïve Bayes, Artificial Neural Network, Decision Tree, and K-Nearest Neighbor algorithms are used in this paper. We also use ensemble methods like Bagging, Adaboosting, and Random Forest to get more accuracy. An ensemble filtering technique has been applied to detect misclassified instance from training dataset which improves the accuracy of predicting. In this paper, ensemble filtering technique gives the best accuracy of 84.3 percent where adaboosting on Artificial Neural Network gives 78.6 percent accuracy.

articleTitle: Improved Feature Extraction Using Segmented FPCA for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Remote sensing hyperspectral image (HSI) retains significant information of ground surface which is actually acquired as a set of hundreds narrow and contiguous spectral bands. Though it is quite difficult to extract features from these bands, dimensionality reduction techniques through feature extraction and feature selection are used to improve the classification performance of the HSI. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is the commonly adopted feature extraction technique for dimensionality reduction of HSI. However, PCA can be failure to extract local characteristics of the HSI due to considering global variance. Thus, segmented-PCA (SPCA) and folded-PCA (FPCA) are introduced to effectively extract the local structures in different ways. In this paper, feature extraction using FPCA, termed as segmented FPCA (SFPCA), has been improved through applying it on the highly correlated bands' segments of the real HSI rather than not applying on the whole dataset directly. The feature selection over the new transformed features was carried out using cumulative-variance accumulation based approach. The experimental result shows that the classification accuracy of SFPCA (95.6262%) outperforms conventional FPCA (95.1292%), SPCA (93.837%) and PCA (93.7376%). Moreover, it provides the least space complexity.

articleTitle: An analysis of Feature extraction and Classification Algorithms for Dangerous Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: One of the important practical applications of object detection and image classification can be for security enhancement. If dangerous objects e.g. knives can be identified automatically, then a lot of violence can be prevented. For this purpose, various different algorithms and methods are out there that can be used. In this paper, four of them have been investigated to find out which can identify knives from a dataset of images more accurately. Among Bag of Words, HOG-SVM, CNN and pre-trained Alexnet CNN, the deep learning CNN methods are found to give best results, though they consume significantly more resources.

articleTitle: An Improved MPPT Technique – Alternative to Fractional Open Circuit Voltage Method
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper discusses an improved constant voltage based maximum power point tracking method for extracting maximum power from photovoltaic (PV) system. The improved method has better performance than the conventional fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) method. By calculating accurate maximum power point voltage for any changing environmental conditions, the improved method can determine maximum power more accurately. MATLAB/Simulink has been used to implement a PV module (considering a single diode model). Simulation results are analyzed for variable solar irradiance to compare the performance of these two methods.

articleTitle: Application of DC Chopper to Augment Fault Ride Through of DFIG Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Transient analysis is an important feature of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG). In this paper, for enhancing fault ride through (FRT) capability of DFIG based wind turbine a DC chopper is used which is connected across the DC-link capacitor. Two schemes were observed; the first scheme uses one insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) switch in series with a resistor to show the effect of the DC chopper magnitude. In this scheme, the best DC chopper resistor was obtained. The second scheme uses a circuit breaker to determine the best insertion time and duration of operation of the DC chopper. Proposed schemes were applied to a DFIG to investigate the transient analysis. Simulations were done by using PSCAD/EMTDC software. Simulation results show the DC chopper can adequately improve the FRT capability of the DFIG and also show the DC chopper resistor should be chosen carefully, because during a grid fault the large value may affect the system performance.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Three Phase Inverters with Different Types of PWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: To utilize the renewable energy sources efficiently, inverter is a fundamental device. A large amount of power is lost due to switching and harmonic effect. So to accumulate the energy and increase the efficiency of power inverter, an optimum point should be determined which will reduce the switching loss and harmonic effect. The aim of this paper is to ascertain the optimum condition. This paper studies about four basic types of pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques using MATLAB/Simulink software. These techniques help to reduce the harmonics component and hence the total harmonic distortion (THD) is minimized. The techniques we have studied are sine PWM (SPWM), third harmonic injected PWM (THPWM), sixty degree PWM (SDPWM) and trapezoidal PWM (TRPWM). We have tried to suggest which PWM technique is better among them by varying the frequency of the carrier signal and modulation index. This study also suggests the optimum condition for which the THD and switching loss is minimum.

articleTitle: Efficient Duty Cycle Management for Reduction of Energy Consumption in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN) is a strapping combination of inexpensive, diminutive, computational and communication impelled sensor nodes which are powered by irreplaceable battery. So the lifetime of a sensor node is fixed. This lifetime can be increased only by using proper management of power consumption. Duty cycle based energy management scheme is very efficient medium access control (MAC) protocol of the WSN which effectively conserve energy of sensor nodes. In this paper, we propose a new management scheme for the duty cycle based MAC protocol to reduce the energy consumption by the sensor nodes as well as improve the network lifetime. In the proposed scheme, the total duty cycle is divided into two equal parts, one part is used for transmission of own data and another part is used for transmission/reception of neighbor node's data. If there is no data available for either own or neighbor nodes then it will go to the sleep mode during that part of duty cycle to save the energy consumption. The performance of the proposed protocol is evaluated by numerical simulations. From the simulation results it is confirmed that the proposed scheme provides lower energy consumption as well as higher lifetime than the existing scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Wireless Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In order to reduce pressure on fossil fuel and reduce environmental pollution, the use of electric vehicles (EV) is rapidly increasing, instead of combustion engine vehicles. The main concern issue of the EV customers is being addressed through various charging methods. The key difficulty in implementation of EV is arrangement of charging infrastructure. The wireless charging system (WCS) is a favorite option in the growing EV market. In this paper, a WCS for charging electric vehicles is developed via inductively coupled power transfer technology. A simulation system is made in the MATLAB/SIMULINK, and the performance of the system is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Circural Planner Inverted-F Antenna for Implantable Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: A circular-shaped planner inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is proposed at 2.45 GHz for implantable medical devices in Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) bands. The proposed antenna has the radius of 8.5 mm. The antenna is simulated using CST microwave suite. To minimize the dimension of the antenna and to enhance performance, meandering technique employed. The coaxial feed is used for the proposed antenna and shorting pin is placed at suitable position to match the input impedance to 50 Ω coaxial cable. A dielectric substrate of FR-4 of dielectric constant (εr) of 4.3 and loss transient (δ) of 0.025 with a thickness of 1.5 mm is used. The simulated resonance frequency is 2.45 GHz with a bandwidth of 47.4 MHz (2.4285 GHz - 2.4759 GHz) at return loss - 10 dB in free space. Moreover, a biocompatible material of silica is coated around the antenna to work in biological tissues. Then, to validate biocompatibility, the antenna performance is evaluated in the phantom model.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Vehicle Communication Using RF and IR Technology
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In the urban areas, most of the sound pollution are caused because of noisy environment which is created by industrial machineries and vehicle horn. Among all the reasons the vehicle horn is assumed most vital for making the noisy environment which has a hazardous impact on the human health. Therefore, it is become graver to need a system that is able to make the environment safe and sound. To confront this challenge, this study proposes a V2V or Vehicle to Vehicle Communication System. In this study, the V2V Communication has been accomplished using both Infrared and radio frequency communication without using horn. IR transmitter which is used to transmit the signal to front side vehicles and RF transmitter which is used to transmit the signal to both left and right side vehicles are placed in front of the driver. Moreover, IR and RF receivers are inserted behind the car to receive the corresponding transmitted signal from the other vehicles. A speaker is used to alert the driver and a LCD is used to show from where the transmitted signal has been come and the driver will decide where the car should be moved. The whole functions of the system are processed by PIC Microcontroller. The goal of this work is to mitigate the vehicle noise to some extent and to reduce unnecessary vehicle horn. This system can be used as a substitution of horn system in the populated, emergency and busy places.

articleTitle: A New 36-Pulse Diode Rectifier with Two Passive Injection Circuits
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new 36-pulse diode rectifier for harmonic mitigation. The proposed rectifier consists of a parallel 12-pulse diode rectifier and two passive injection circuits. The first injection circuit consists of modified specially tapped interphase transformer (MSTIT) with two additional diodes and the second injection circuit consists of single phase diode rectifier (SFDR). These passive injection circuits triple the number of pulses of the parallelly connected rectifier. The proposed rectifier eliminates lower than 35<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order harmonics from the utility line currents. The proposed rectifier requires lower components than that of other rectifier circuits with similar performance. The proposed rectifier is suitable for high current rating rectifiers such as electrochemical processes, induction heating, plasma torches etc. In this paper, the operation of the proposed rectifier is explained, analyzed and simulated.

articleTitle: Determining the optimum tilt angle and orientation for photovoltaic (PV) systems in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Tilt angle of a PV module is one of the most significant parameters for receiving maximum solar irradiation falling on the PV systems. This research article investigates the numerical aspects of selecting the optimal tilt angle for the PV modules used in Bangladesh and makes recommendations on how the collected power output of the module can be increased by altering the tilt angle. The results show that the optimum tilt angle of Cox's Bazzar Chittagong, Dhaka, Jessore, Ishurdi, Bogra, Sylhet and Rangpur is 26°, 25°, 30°, 25°, 27°, 27°, 28° and 29°, respectively. The annual energy production of Cox's Bazar and Sylhet has shown the highest and the lowest energy production, the month was March and July, respectively. The characteristics curves obtained by the simulation with the data provided by using simulated software SAM (System Advisor Model). Finally, the article measures the optimum tilt for PV applications in Bangladesh on Monthly and yearly bases.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition based on Support Vector Machine using Gabor Wavelet Filter
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Face is the most important part of human body. Facial expression is a way of nonverbal communication with one another. Human face expresses the internal emotional feelings and contains important information. It is our goal to extract considerable features used for real-time Facial Expression Recognition (FER) system. Facial expression can be recognized by both facial shape features and appearance features. In our proposed methodology, we first extract the shape features from positions on a face. Then multi-orientation Gabor wavelet coefficient feature are extracted from expression images. We have used Support Vector Machines (SVM) as classifier. As face has some fixed special points, linear classifier works excellent on facial point data. Thus SVM performs with satisfactory outcomes in our FER system. Our experimental result shows that using facial shape features and Gabor wavelet coefficient based on SVM is more accurate and faster most other previously proposed methodologies.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Rectangular, Circular and Elliptical Shape Microstrip Patch Antenna using Coaxial Probe Feed
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, various shapes of microstrip patch antenna that means rectangular, circular, elliptical patch have been designed to investigate the performances of the different shapes of patch of microstrip antenna. These antennas are designed with coaxial probe feed. FR4_epoxy is utilized as the substrate material of these antennas whose relative permittivity is 4.4. The return loss, bandwidth, Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR), gain, directivity, efficiency all are simulated utilizing ansoft HFSS software that are worked in C-band application having resonant frequency at 5 GHz. A relative report has been made among the three patches to see the impact of different shapes of patch.

articleTitle: Extraction of Linear and Non-Linear Features of Electrocardiogram Signal and Classification
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: ECG signal for a private creature is totally different because of the distinctive heart structure. The ambition of feature extraction of electrocardiogram signal would permit productive detection of irregularities and economic projection due to any kind of heart confusion. Some dominant feature options are going to be extracted from ECG signals namely frequency, mean, median, skewness, kurtosis, standard deviation, different kinds of norms and so on. So, there is a need for strong and robust mathematical model to extract such helpful parameters. This research work is related to an associate degree reconciling mathematical analysis model i.e. Hilbert Huang Transform (HHT). The Hilbert-Huang transform technique is enforced to evaluate the nonlinear and non-stationary representation of the graphical signal. It is distinctive and totally disparate from the current ways of investigation and will not crave a prior function supporting information. The efficiency of the planned theme is confirmed through different classification techniques.

articleTitle: Comparison of Noninvasive Heart Rate Monitoring System using GSM Module and RF Module
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: New innovations and the latest technology has brought about revolutionary changes in the branch of medical science enabling us to be more enthusiastic about health monitoring system. As people are more prone to cardiovascular diseases now-a-days, innovative heart rate monitoring system has now been getting popular. But only monitoring system is not enough in case of emergency need of medication and treatment. During cardiac arrest cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be administered by a trained person. For this reason a message is needed to be sent to an authorized person or a doctor. This paper focuses on measuring heart rate with Arduino and sensor using noninvasive method with sending an emergency and urgent message via Global System for Mobile (GSM) communication module and radio frequency (RF) module, and a comparison between the two modules is made with respect of speed, reliability and cost.

articleTitle: A Novel Regenerative Braking System of BLDC Motor for Lightweight Electric Vehicles: An Analysis of Braking Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper a novel regenerative braking mechanism based on Brushless DC (BLDC) motor is proposed. Based on proposed method braking can be achieved by applying different Stator voltage from a multi cell battery system without using additional DC-DC boost converter with complex switching technique or ultra-capacitor. To evaluate the performance of the proposed braking system an experimental setup has been used. Simulated results prove that the proposed regenerative braking technique is feasible and efficient. Also this research provides simplest system for regenerative braking using BLDC motor to improve the mileage of lightweight electric vehicles (EVs).

articleTitle: An Artificial Neural Network Based Predictive Approach for Analyzing Environmental Impact on Combined Cycle Power Plant Generation
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Global climate has gone through a drastic change in the recent few decades. Besides human life it has imposed a great threat on the different industries. One of the major victims of this threat is electric power generation industry. This is what motivates this study to analyze how and to what extent the environment can harm the power generation sector. This study concentrates on combined cycle power plant generation and a detailed analysis has been done using Artificial Neural Network(ANN) as a data processing tool in Matlab environment. This study shows a top to bottom strategy to deal with this type of supervised learning problems where dataset plays an inevitable part for this type of analysis. So, to prepare a proper dataset in this study an IoT based device for automatic data logging has been used.

articleTitle: Battery Impedance Measurement Using Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Board
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Battery internal impedance reflects the dynamic behavior in their continuous operation. Impedance measurement is an important issue in order to extend the battery run time, determine the parameter loss factors related to the thermal rise, and obtain more frequently updated parameters of the battery for better utilization. The battery online impedance measurement is also a crucial parameter to estimate the battery state of charge. The real time circuit has difficulties due to circuit complexity, implement at low cost and extract the low ranges ac ripple voltage response due to ac excitation. This paper proposed a simple way to extract the battery ac ripple contents using real time circuit topology for measuring the battery impedance. The compatibility and usability of different voltage measurement also investigated in this paper for measuring the low ranges battery ac ripple voltage. The analog filter circuit extracts the battery ac ripple voltage and current, the zero crossing and peak detector circuits detect the peak and zero crossing point respectively. The circuit simulation result shows that, the real time circuit based electrochemical impedance spectroscopy board can be designed at low cost and integrated into smart battery management system for assessing the internal characteristics of a battery regularly.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Different Wireless Power Transfer Circuits
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) means, transmission of electrical energy without any wire (or physical contact). In this paper, four WPT circuits have been designed and simulated using MATLAB/Simulink and Multisim. The first & second circuits are based on inductive coupling and they have both transmitter and receiver section. But the last two circuits have only receiver section and they can be used for harvesting ambient radio frequency (RF) energy. The first two circuits were simulated using both MATLAB/Simulink & Multisim but the last two circuits were simulated only in Multisim.

articleTitle: Efficient Data Embedding for Interpolation based Reversible Data Hiding Scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Interpolation based reversible data hiding (RDH) has showed great promises for better embedding rate-distortion performance in digital image applications. In this paper, we develop and present a quadratic interpolation based RDH scheme, where all the embeddable bits are sought to be effectively utilized to ensure a minimum possible embedding distortion with higher embedding capacity. Particularly, unlike a recent interpolation based RDH scheme, the proposed embedding process avoids the use of flag bit to track whether the embedded payload-bits are in original or complement form. This tracking is achieved by utilizing the correlation between the embeddable pixel and estimated versions of embedded pixel and thereby one more data bit is embedded in place of the flag bit. The early results of our proposed scheme compared to recent IRDH schemes have recorded a significantly higher embedding capacity (i.e., 42% and 46% higher bpp) with better image quality (i.e., 1.4% and 2.25% higher PSNR, and 5.57% and 2.74% higher SSIM) for similar values of capacity control parameter, respectively.

articleTitle: Crowd Reckoning towards Preventing the Repeat of ‘2015 Hajj Pilgrims Stampede’
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The issue of crowd reckoning has as of late gotten noteworthy consideration in the current era. Given an image of a crowded environment, the objective is to evaluate the density of the crowd, by counting the quantity of individuals that it contains. There are some approaches to solve crowd reckoning problem. They intend to reckon crowd for a medium sized place. But crowd detection at Hajj Pilgrimage site has never been tried before as far we have studied. Hajj Pilgrimage sites are different than most of the places. The aim of this work is to prevent any future stampede at Hajj Pilgrimage sites. This paper proposes a method where head detection technique is used for the crowd reckoning. It uses the segmentation of head regions from still images. The crowd reckoning will determine the possibility of a stampede and can alarm the people to take necessary steps. Assessment of the proposed model demonstrates worthy performance in realistic operating conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Partition Based Clustering Algorithms on Iris Image Preprocessing
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Today's life entirely depends on information, and security in information system is an essential term. Now a days various biometric feature like fingerprint, gait, iris, face etc. are used to secure any system and it is more powerful to use biometric feature instead of using other traditional techniques like password, PIN number etc. In automated personal identification system iris recognition technique is the most reliable authentication technique and iris image segmentation step is important to acquire good accuracy in this technique. But noisy image decrease the accuracy and most of the errors occur in non-iris region. So it is better to avoid segmentation errors by excluding non-iris regions from iris image. On the other hand cluster analysis one of the data mining concepts, is very useful for finding similar groups from a data set. So cluster analysis can be used for finding relevant groups from iris image. Basically k-means clustering algorithm used on segmentation step. In this thesis work another two clustering algorithms has been used for iris image preprocessing on segmentation step to cluster most similar objects together so that non-iris region can be reduced and compare their performance with k-means algorithm to find out the better one.

articleTitle: Recognizing Hand-based Actions based on Hip-Joint centered Features using KINECT
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Microsoft Kinect provides skeletal joints to extract different features which can be applied to identify different actions performed by subjects. As human moves, skeletal joints contribute to the movements and human actions are nothing but different types of movements in specific orders. Hand wave, hand shaking, push, pull, clapping, throw, catch these are some hand based actions which are difficult to recognize properly in an automated system. Hip-joint plays a vital role to determine joint-based features from human skeleton, as it is approximately the middle joint of the whole skeleton. The joint relative distances (JRD) and joint relative angles (JRA) are used as principle features in recent action recognition methodologies. In this paper, we have proposed a new methodology based on hip-joint centered features which are based on basic physiological movements that contributes to the decent accuracy in identifying hand based actions.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Stand-alone BDFIG With Compensation From Rotor Speed Observer
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Brushless double-fed induction generator (BDFIG) is the upgrade of conventional double-fed induction generator (DFIG) for needless of the brush and slip ring. It can be used for ship shaft power generator system, in which the BDFIG mainly works at stand-alone state. The encoderless operation can enhance the system's reliability and reduce the cost. This paper proposes a modified sensorless control method of BDFIG which can realize precise phase angle control. That can be important when it is used for connecting the machine to the grid quickly and reliably. A rotor speed observer (RSO) is used to supply the feed-forward compensation. Experimental results are given to prove the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Hybrid Cladding Structured Gold Coated Photonic Crystal Fiber Biosensor Based on Surface Plasmon Resonance
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid cladding structured gold coated photonic crystal fiber (PCF) biosensor based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The performance of the proposed biosensor is analyzed by using finite element method (FEM) based software and MATLAB software environment. In the proposed SPR based PCF biosensor, plasmonic material and sensing layer are placed on the outer layer of the PCF to meet the fabrication challenge. The proposed SPR based PCF biosensor exhibits the wavelength sensitivity of 4500 nm/RIU, amplitude sensitivity of 347 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, sensor resolution of 2.22 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> RIU and high degree of linearity with the sensing ranges from analyte refractive index (RI) of 1.35 to 1.38. Considering high sensitivity, high sensor resolution and high linearity, this proposed SPR based PCF biosensor can be a promising candidate for unknown analyte detection.

articleTitle: Lie Detection from Single Feature of Functional Near Infrared Spectroscopic (fNIRS) Signals
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, an easy but efficient lie detection procedure is proposed. For laboratory investigation, several mock lying protocols and lie detection methods are proposed those are time consuming and complex. In this research, a new method of lie detection is proposed that is able to identify the truth and untruth answer of a participant from a single feature of fNIR (Functional Near-Infrared) signal. In this study, 4 participants performed mock lying protocol by answering some questions and during that time their hemodynamic responses are acquired from prefrontal cortex by fNIR device. By proper signal processing steps, we have found a single time domain feature (slope of deoxygenated hemoglobin (dHb) concentration) from some specific channels (channel 1-4 & 9-12) position that differentiates the brain activities between answering lie and truth. The results are justified by statistical hypothesis with 95% confidence interval (p <; 0.05)). This research work will be helpful for designing the embedded system for lie detection.

articleTitle: Design and Improvement of Pattern Quality in Circularly Polarised Slot Array Antenna for Direct Broadcast Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: A circularly polarised radial line slot array antenna (CP-RLSA) is proposed in this paper for direct broadcast satellite applications. A new design suggestion has been introduced and investigated in this study to improve the performance and pattern quality of the antenna. The antenna is composed of spiral rings on the top plate and made with several thousand of slot pairs. The antenna supports waveguide like structure which is composed of air cavity and dielectric materials. An antenna prototype operating at 20 GHz was designed and simulated. The experimental measurements and simulation results show that the antenna has successfully satisfied the required technical specification. The antenna has achieved a maximum gain of 32.2 dBic at 19.4 GHz. The CP-RLSA antenna has demonstrated an radiation efficiency of 95.3% and a total efficiency of 90.3% at 20 GHz. The antenna has also fulfilled the condition of circular polarisation, i.e. axial ratio is below 3-dB level with appropriate radiation patterns. At the operating frequency 20 GHz, the antenna has achieved a gain of 28.1 dBic with side lobe level as low as -14.4 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Rectangular Patch Antenna Array Using Different Feeding Technique
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In wireless communication system, Patch antenna applicable for the development of low cost, minimal weight and low profile antennas that are capable of maintaining high performance. This paper presents a comparison between rectangular patch antenna arrays using two different feeding techniques: microstrip line feeding and coaxial probe feeding at 2.4 GHz operating frequency. A 2×2 linear array is designed for both line feeding and coaxial probe feeding. Finally, we analyzed the 2×3 linear antenna array to increase directivity, gain, efficiency and better radiation patterns. The substrate used is FR4 with dielectric constant of 4.3 and thickness about 1.6mm. The antenna array is designed and simulated by CST microwave studio.

articleTitle: A survey on students' awareness about e-waste in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: E-waste management is related to recycle, reduce and reuse of electric devices. Although there are no accurate solutions for managing e-waste, almost all the countries in the world have recognized this issue a growing problem and act according to it. In Bangladesh, e-waste is increasing exponentially, although e-waste management is not improved with the demand. Therefore, a large amount of e-waste in the environment is a great threat. A survey has been carried out among students from 3 different cities in Bangladesh to know about their readiness on e-waste management and based on the survey, it has been assessed that there are lots of awareness activities should be performed in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Mitigating Information Disclosure Attacks in the Cloud by Blocking Invalid User and Figure Out Problems to Solve DDoS by Analyzing StackOverflow Questions
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: According to the A10 Networks survey, in 2017 the DDoS of Things (DoT) has reached critical mass in each attack. And the rise of DDoS attacks on cloud computing is commonplace. In this paper, we review and analyze different existing DDoS detecting techniques against different parameters, and propose a new composite architecture to protect AWS infrastructure. The proposed work provides prevention against the DDoS attack on SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) based web services. Our proposed framework check the authenticity of the user, who want to access the data, which is available on the cloud server. And one more thing we reveal in this research that what are the problems facing by the developer and AWS user by the questions they asked recently in Stackoverflow site.

articleTitle: A Review of Multi-pulse AC-DC Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a detail investigation of different types of the converter with and without the transformer from low to high voltage range, and different types of converter harmonic reduction techniques. It is well known that during power conversion some harmonics is generated that is very harmful to electrical equipment. In this work, some multi-pulse insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) based power converter has been simulated with and without static filter capacitors. The performance among those has been compared. Main objectives of this work are to investigate a suitable converter with lower cost, complexity, total harmonic distortion (THD) and voltage/current ripple. Simulation work has been done by using MATLAB/Simulink environment and a dc motor is connected to output side as a load. The obtained results have been discussed in detail to justify the validity of the review result. Finally, some possibilities to improve this research have been mentioned.

articleTitle: Security in Nakagami-m Fading Channel with Log-normal Shadowing
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a confidential communication scenario is considered through composite Nakagami-m fading channel with log-normal shadowing in which a source communicates with a destination in the presence of an eavesdropper. Our study is concerned with the analysis of secrecy capacity and secure outage performance of Nakagami-m fading channel with shadowing. The performance of the proposed model is analyzed based on the closed-form expressions of the ergodic secrecy capacity, the probability of non-zero secrecy capacity and the secure outage probability using the Gauss-Hermite quadrature integration formula. Analytical results show that the shadowing effect significantly enhances the ergodic secrecy capacity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of A Textile Antenna Working at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible textile antenna working at 2.4GHz suitable for wireless body area networks. The antenna is composed of leather and copper tape. Such simple structure makes the antenna flexible, cheap and easy to be reproduced. The antenna has been simulated in CST microwave studio. A prototype of the proposed antenna is also fabricated. Numerical and measured results are compared in terms of reflection coefficient. Performances are also evaluated in terms of voltage standing wave ratio, radiation pattern and directivity. The antenna offers a 4.27dB gain with 64.65% radiation efficiency. Performance of the antenna near human body has also been monitored. It is observed that the resonant frequency shifts downward when the antenna is placed on the human body.

articleTitle: Novel Multirate Digital Filter for EEG on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: A new denoising multirate system method of using field-programmable gate array (FPGA) chip for bio-chip design & implementation of EEG signal is appeared in this article. The ALTERA Cyclone II FPGA board development board implements this bio-chip in real-time with processors EP2C35F672C6 for the proper data accuracy. Modelsim is used for simulation of biochip design in Verilog HDL. In this paper denoising on multirate system is used with support of up-sampler or interpolate, moving average filter and downs-sampler or decimator for removing of noise by bio-chip. This biochip shows good enough electrical characteristics such as less area and power, low voltage & current, enough memory storage spaces, null delay.

articleTitle: Advancements of Air, Water and Nanofluid Based Photovoltaic Thermal (PV/T) Technologies
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: At present world, due to the increasing demand of heat and electrical energy, photovoltaic thermal (PV/T) systems have become very popular to the modern researchers. The PV/T system generates heat and electricity simultaneously. To obtain more electric power and thermal energy from the PV/T systems, PV cell cooling is very important. Usually air and liquid are used as heat carrying medium to cool the PV panels. In commercial market, efficient PV/T systems are not available. From the last few decades, several researchers are working on the PV/T systems to increase the system performance. This paper describes the development of conventional and newly designed air, water and nanofluid based PV/T systems.

articleTitle: Indemnity for Frequency Disruption in a Smart Grid during Cyber–Attack
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Indemnity for frequency disruption in smart grid system due to cyber-attack is essential to avoid unstable power supply which can cause severe blackout. In this paper, a protective model is proposed for providing robust control of frequency in any situation, especially during cyber-attack on automatic generation control. A controlled switching unit is included in the protective model for ensuring protection against disruptive frequency during cyber-attack. The proposed control scheme restores frequency two times faster than the existing method.

articleTitle: A Forward Kinematics approach towards Humanoid Robot handwriting
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Robot handwriting can be a useful and reliable method of receiving feedback from Humanoid Robots in environments where there are barriers to traditional speech synthesis techniques. It can also provide as an indispensable tool for aid in teaching and also in communicating with people having hearing disabilities. However, there are certain issues such as kinematic redundancy and the degrees of freedom problem that make robot handwriting difficult to implement. This study details the development of a Forward Kinematics approach to overcome these setbacks. The NAO Humanoid robot has been used as a model platform for testing and simulation of these algorithms. Kinematic equations have been derived for the NAO robot's right-arm and the theoretical joint angle parameters are then fed into the developed Choregraphe application for simulating the results. Additionally, the number of actively rotating joints has been minimized to reduce the chances of inducing motor fatigue. The handwriting results and optimization techniques have been enhanced and finally verified using motion curves.

articleTitle: RFID Based Hospital Laboratory Automation System
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In recent years, high expectations for the integration of RFID in healthcare scenarios have emerged. Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology meets identification and tracking requirements in healthcare environments. It has the potential to speed up and increase reliability of the processes. The objective of this research work is to develop an automation system for hospital's laboratory. The system uses RFID tags attached with the samples collected from the patients for identification. Smart cards are used to store patient's data and the whole system is run under a work station which monitors the process.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Double Layer Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a double layer rectangular microstrip patch antenna array for ISM band applications. The proposed antenna gives higher gain and directivity maintaining same size as single layer rectangular microstrip patch antenna (RMPA) array. Design and simulations are done at center frequency 5.8 GHz in CST software. The gain and directivity of RMPA is 9.42 dB and 9.56 dBi respectively. Whereas 10.30 dB gain and 10.48 dBi directivity are obtained from double layer RMPA array. This significant improved performance of double layer rectangular microstrip patch antenna array can be used in WLAN applications and real time implementation.

articleTitle: Rate-Distortion Analysis of an Improved Pixel Value Ordering based Reversible Embedding
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an improvement of a prominent Pixel Value Ordering (PVO)-based Reversible Data Hiding (RDH) scheme. We started with analyzing the rate-distortion performance of the scheme for different neighborhood pixels. Particularly, unlike an image block with horizontal neighborhood pixels considered in that scheme, we proposed a set of blocks of size 3× 2 (or 2× 3) that creates a pair of pixels-trios. In a pixels-trio, two pixels in one row and the third pixel immediately under or above of the other two pixels form a triangular shaped block. This allows a greater possible correlation among the pixels resulting in higher embedding rate with lower possible distortion. We also investigated the case of 3× 1 size blocks with vertical neighborhood pixels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed embedding technique with 2× 3 size blocks offers the best rate-distortion performance for USC-SIPI image-set compared to the original scheme and embedding with other block sizes.

articleTitle: Loosely Coupled GPS/INS Integrated Navigation System based on Kalman Filter and Complementary Filter for Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: GPS/INS integrated system provides more precise position of an aircraft compared to individual system. The objective of this paper is to propose a loosely coupled GPS/INS integrated system with Kalman Filter (KF) and Complementary Filter (CF). The integration has been carried out in two techniques. Firstly the systems are integrated using KF. Secondly, the same is done applying both KF and CF. In this paper, a comparative study of these two techniques is addressed with the help of MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Investigation of Semiconductor Doped B6 Nanocluster: A First Principle Study
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Borophene, a new addition in 2D nanomaterial family, has recently gain huge interest because of its superior band engineering properties unlike its 2D counterpart, graphene. We have investigated various properties and also some important physical indices of Borophene, as represented by the B6 nanocluster, and compare the undoped and Germanium-doped B6 motif using DFT method with SDD basis set and B3LYP level of theory. For studying the charge transfer between the B6 nanocluster and the dopant, we calculated Mulliken charge for two different doped-structures namely, pyramidal (GeB6) and bi-pyramidal (Ge2B6). The DOS spectra analysis shows the difference between the HOMO and LUMO energies. We have made here a conventional correlation among adsorption energy, energy gap, hardness, softness, chemical potential and electrophilicity. The bi-pyramidal structure of Ge doped B6 nanocluster shows better stability as evident by the adsorption energy.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Binary Polarization Shift Keying OCDMA FSO System under Different Atmospheric Conditions
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of a binary polarization shift keying optical code division multiple access (BPolSK-OCDMA) free space optical (FSO) system is investigated in terms of bit error rate (BER) and Q factor under the influence of different atmospheric conditions like clear air, rain, fog, snow etc. It is found that system performance is highly dependent on transmission length and different atmospheric conditions such as fog, rain, snow etc. However, among the atmospheric parameters, the system performance is found to be highly affected under foggy condition.

articleTitle: An Efficient Multi-Thread Polling based DBA Algorithm for Solving the Over-Granting Problem of Long-Reach PON
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The expansion of passive optical network (PON) system into long reach PON (LR-PON) introduced large propagation delay if conventional Report and Grant messages scheduling schemes are used. Without sophisticated arrangement of Report-Grant scheduling, the LR-PON system may suffer from the over-granting problem. Due to this over-granting problem, the overall performance of the LR-PON can affect by overlapping of time slots, requesting same data twice and unused time slots. In this paper, we propose a new Report and Grant scheduling scheme to reduce the over-granting problem with a delay reduction principle. In the existing multi-thread polling (MTP) based DBA algorithms, if the Reported bytes are not matched with the maximum granted window size then it transmits smaller data byte by lower rounding of queued frames and introduced over-granting problem. In the proposed DBA algorithm, all the queued frames information are reported by the ONUs and OLT Grants the number of frames with window size to avoid the over-granting problem. The proposed scheme also distributes the Granted window size among the ONUs based on the fair bandwidth demands. We compare the performance of the proposed scheme with the existing STP and MTP schemes. The comparative result shows that the proposed scheme reduces almost 45% of the average packet delay at maximum offered load 1.0 compared to the existing MTP scheme. The simulation results also show that the proposed scheme provides higher throughput and bandwidth utilization performance than the existing schemes.

articleTitle: The planar B6 cluster as a motif for doping metal cation (Al3+): A DFT study
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This present research investigation reports various properties of doped and undoped boron cluster (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) such as charge distribution, stability, adsorption energy, dipole moment, reactivity, vibrational frequency, optical property, orbital analysis etc. on the basis of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> motif, which is actually the hexagonal vacancy of borophene (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">36</sub>) cluster. We have used the density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/SDD level of theory. At first, we have studied the properties of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> motif and then Al-doped B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> cluster with pyramidal and bi-pyramidal geometries have been investigated and compared them with the planar B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> motif.

articleTitle: I-Ranger: A voice controlled environment inspection roverbot with live video streaming and mechanical gripper
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Human-robot interaction is an important, attractive and challenging area. In this research an android based robot was designed and implemented that has the characteristics of functioning on voice commands; riding through rough and rugged tracks; sensing temperature, humidity, gas and smoke; detecting obstacles; picking objects and performing surveillance. The developed robotic system was also equipped with a built-in radar system that can give out an approximate vision of its surroundings. Wireless communication system has been used to communicate with the robot for sending commands to and receiving required information and data from the robot. In absence of wireless communication, it can also run in autonomous mode. To make the module be able to traverse through rough grounds caterpillar track was included.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement of DFIG and PMSG Based Hybrid Wind Farm Using SMES
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The reserve of fossil fuel is decreasing and the energy consumption rate is increasing day by day. To meet this increasing energy demand without polluting and warming the world, renewable energy sources are adopted for producing electricity. Wind is one of the most promising renewable energy sources and the use of this source has been increasing very fast. This paper deals with the simulation of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) and Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) wind turbine based hybrid wind power generation system equipped with SMES in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. The DFIG based and PMSG based wind power systems are simulated separately. Then they are connected parallel and combined. The variable wind speed is taken as the input of the turbine. The simulation results show that the system with SMES provides more quality power than the system without SMES.

articleTitle: H-Bridge Driven Propulsion System for a Light Weight Electric Vehicle using DC Link Voltage Controller
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel and simple method for H-bridge driven propulsion System using a DC motor for a Light Weight Electric Vehicle (LEV) such as Three-wheeler. For controlling the motor, an H-Bridge driven system is introduced which is incorporated with an optimized DC Link voltage controller while placing the DC motor in the load. The direction of the motor will depend based on the switching combinations of the H-bridge drive. Proposed DC Link voltage controller is used to keep the output voltage of the controller constant by varying the duty cycle of a bi-direction boost converter as per the input voltage command. The output voltage of the controller is converted into speed which is provided as input speed of the motor. Maintaining the same speed command, the armature current and output speed of the motor is analyzed in various conditions. The H-bridge drive along with the DC Link voltage controller has been simulated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Prediction of Disorder of Brain using EEG Signal Processing in MATLAB GUI Platform
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) records electrical activity of the brain. In this paper, a user-friendly platform using MATLAB with GUI (Graphical User Interface) is designed for analyzing EEG data and spotting patterns in it for fast diagnosis purposes. At first the noise is omitted by using a Butterworth low pass and FIR bandpass filter respectively and then explored to determine power spectral density. Several parameters (mean, variance, skewness and kurtosis) are extracted from the diagrams of power spectral density and contour of the peaks. It is seen that mean is high and skewness and kurtosis are low for affected brain. The relationship can be more useful to find out the presence of any disorder in brain.

articleTitle: CdTe Thin Film Fabrication by Thermal Evaporation Technique
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Cadmium Telluride thin film has been prepared by thermal vacuum evaporation technique on soda lime glass substrate. Cadmium Telluride is very potential III-V material higher efficiency in coming days and it has been recognized as a promising material for thin film solar application. Existing material for thin film solar cell production is the p-CdTe/n-CdS/TCO/glass substrate. Two thin film of thickness 300 nm and 400nm were deposited by thermal vacuum evaporation technique. X-Ray diffractometry of these films were taken to be sure that as deposited thin films are deposited by CdTe. The peak diffraction intensity of 300nm thin film was found at 23.85 degree and for 400nm thin film peak it was found at 23.87 degree this result confirms us that the two films are CdTe.

articleTitle: Modified Square Lattice Photonic Crystal Fiber (SLPCF) Incorporating EDFA and Definite Power CW Laser for Improved RoF Link
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this work, a modified SLPCF Radio-over-fiber (RoF) link incorporating erbium doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) and continuous wave (CW) laser of definite power is proposed as a new approach of forward error correction (FEC). In particular, the RoF model operates with CW laser driven at 1 dBm, 10 dBm and 15 dBm input powers. The model is simulated considering 1010 bit sequence and the results are compared with those using conventional SMF and previously described SLPCF configuration. We observed that the proposed RoF link produces reduced dispersion and BER, sharper eye diagram and both the improved Q-factor and eye height. Thus, the performance of the RoF link using modified SLPCF incorporating EDFA and CW laser definite power is noticeably improved, therefore, the model can be useful for cost-effective RoF link design.

articleTitle: A Simplistic, Effective, and Adaptive Approach towards Classifying Medical Records according to ICD-10 using Machine Learning for Efficient Statistics
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Maintaining medical records is essential in the perspective of modern medical science. The medical record is a legal document of treatment received by the patient, as well as it indicates the quality of service provided by the hospital. For research and innovation, it is the source of raw data. Moreover, it contributes valuable information to the medical surveys. Therefore, the proper use of data stored in medical records has prime importance. In this regard, the data must be arranged logically so that necessary information is available on demand. This paper proposes to classify these data logically and systematically while keeping the identity of the patients confidential. However, with the advancement of medical science, medical records are also becoming more complex. We have used machine learning in order to solve the problem instead of conventional coding schemes so that the program can adapt itself autonomously with new information over time.

articleTitle: Outage Performance Analysis for Multicasting with Opportunistic Relaying
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a multicast scenario is considered through selection decode-and-forward cooperative relay networks over Nakagami-m fading channel in which a source communicates with multiple destinations via multiple cooperative relays. A best relay is selected using selection combining technique which communicates with the destinations. The performance of the proposed model is analyzed based on the closed-form expression of the outage probability. Analytical results reveal that the additional diversity provided by the best relay significantly improves the outage performance of the proposed model mitigating the fading severity of wireless channel.

articleTitle: A low cost obstacle avoiding autonomous vehicle with Global Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Autonomous vehicle is a self-driving vehicle and does not require any operator to navigate and accomplish its task. The purpose of this paper is to develop such a vehicle which can not only detect an object in front of it but also be able to avoid it. So, it is equipped with ultrasonic sensor to detect the objects in its path and it also has a Global Positioning System (GPS) module and compass to determine its current position and navigate it to a designated location. After developing the proposed vehicle system, it has been examined that it is able to reach a predefined location while avoiding obstacle in its path. The autonomous vehicle made for the purpose of this study was also made with cheaper sensors, making it more viable for the general consumers. This autonomous vehicle system is expected to bring a degree of autonomy in the currently deployed user controlled vehicles for developing countries. It will also have many practical implementations in daily and military life.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a PV Power Generating System Using MMC Converter and High Frequency Magnetic Link
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: At present, PV power generating system (PVPGS) has become an emerging field of research. Many technologies have been developed to reduce the cost and improve the efficiency of this system. Modular multilevel cascade (MMC) converter and high frequency magnetic link (HFML) are two such technologies, which have reduced the cost and several challenges of this system. Here, a MATLAB simulation of a PVPGS using MMC converter and HFML is shown. It is observed that due to use of MMC converter, the output voltage is improved and due to use of HFML the size and cost can also be reduced.

articleTitle: Developing Poly-Mask for Automatic ROI Selection of Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Region-of-Interest (ROI) or Region-of-Non-Interest (RONI) selection is a key step in medical image (MI) watermarking to avoid any concern of possible incorrect diagnosis from watermarked MIs. Generally, an automatic ROIs/RONIs selection is an ever challenging task due to the variety of locations and shapes of ROIs/RONIs in different modality MIs. In this paper, we have developed and presented Poly-Mask, an algorithm for automatic selection of ROIs. Poly-Mask takes an input MI, processes it morphologically and computes a polygonal mask, poly-ROI that captures the ROIs by using convex-hull without consideration of any basic shape used in earlier methods. A minimum information (e.g., values of vertices, minimum and maximum axes) is then determined for directly regenerating the poly-ROI later for watermark embedding and extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Poly-Mask algorithm can select and accurately generate the poly-ROIs and so the ROIs/RONIs of different MIs, which can be used for different MI watermarking applications.

articleTitle: FIR Filter Design Using an Adjustable Spectral Efficient Window Function
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a new adjustable window function, combined by Blackman and Lanczos window functions, has been proposed. The spectral properties and the shape of the proposed window can be adjusted by changing the value of the controlling parameter. The spectral properties of the proposed window have been cpmpared with Gaussian, Lanczos and Kaiser Windows. From MATLAB simulation results, it is observed that the proposed window provides better ripple ratio than Gaussian and Lanczos windows and better side-lobe roll-off ratio than Kaiser and Gaussian windows. In order to justify the performance of the proposed window function, it has been applied to design Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters. The MATLAB simulation results have confirmed that the filters designed by the proposed window provide better spectral properties and better gain than the other preceding windows.

articleTitle: Efficient Rectenna Design for Harvesting Microwave Power from SSPS System
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to design an efficient and simple ground based rectenna system for receiving microwave power. The performance of designed system is tested in Advanced Design System (ADS) simulation environment. This system can receive microwave power from Space Solar Power Satellite (SSPS) system and convert microwave energy into Direct Current (DC). The ground based rectenna consists of microstrip patch antenna array with rectifier circuit using Schottky diode. The rectifier circuit consists of low pass filter, diode, matching circuit and Dickson charge pump voltage multiplier circuit. This multiplier circuit increases output voltage considering small input power. In this paper, 8 elements microstrip patch antenna array operated at 2.45 GHz frequency with high efficient rectifier circuit is designed. The simulation results show better gain and directivity of proposed rectenna system which increase the performance of existing SSPS systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis for Liquid Based Thermoelectric Electronic Cooling (LTEEC) System
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this research work, an experimental analysis has been done with a liquid based thermoelectric electronic cooling system, using two developed aluminium heat exchangers. An Ethylene-Glycol based fluid was used as the coolant in the cooling system. A modified cooling module was used for the proposed electronic cooling system. Both numerical analysis using COMSOL Multiphysics and experimental work were performed to investigate a better heat exchanger for the system. It is found that the large aluminium heat exchanger shows better performance compared to the small one. The commercially found cooling system performed the worst performance. The temperature variation was between 29-30 °C, which is nearly 2 °C less than the commercial cooling system and showed steady performance.

articleTitle: Electronic and Vibrational Properties of Single Layer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDC)
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Two dimensional (2D) layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDC) have recently attracted remarkable attention due to their direct and wide band gap. These semiconductor materials can be used in electronics device and in optoelectronic devices. In semiconductor materials the electronic and vibrational properties play a fundamental role in device characterization in consequently many physical observables specifically thermal and transport properties. Here the structural optimization, electronic properties and vibrational properties of tungsten disulfide (WS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) have been calculated by the first principle Calculation based on density functional Theory (DFT) which is implemented on the quantum espresso. The direct band gap of WS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> have been found at K point from the DFT calculations are 1.98 eV and 1.9 eV. The high frequency optical phonon modes are separated from the low frequency optical phonon modes by a gap of 207 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for single-layer WS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and 285 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for single-layer MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> respectively.

articleTitle: Designing of a Plasmonic High Pass Wavelength Filter With Apodized Grating Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a nanoscale plasmonic high pass filter is proposed using metal-insulator-metal (MIM) waveguide consisting of inward and outward grating profiles which are apodized by super Gaussian function. The frequency dependent model of the metal is developed using Lorentz-Drude model which is solved numerically using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation in order to calculate the transmission efficiency of the filter. Both inward and outward gratings are simulated individually and compared. It has been found that the cut-off wavelength can be controlled precisely with the variation of the maximum grating width. Moreover, the proposed design is easier to fabricate since the simple geometrical shape is proposed.

articleTitle: Stability Enhancement of Grid-Connected DFIG with GA Optimized PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This work presents an efficient application of the genetic algorithm for improving the small signal dynamic performance of grid-integrated (Doubly Fed Induction Generator) DFIG system fed by wind energy. The nonlinear differential-algebraic model of DFIG based system has been presented and linearization is performed for obtaining the small signal dynamic model. Eigenvalue analysis and time domain based simulations are presented for visualizing the results. The obtained result is compared with the PI controllers whose parameters are chosen based on trial-and-error method. The optimized results with genetic algorithm show that the system shows far better performance than PI controller without GA.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Electromagnetic Field Radiation for Engineering Workshop using Three Axis Tesla Meter
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents measurement and analysis of electromagnetic field radiation for engineering workshop using three-axis Tesla meter. The measurements are carried out at the exposure level of power frequency magnetic field in some typical places where the workers are subjected to the fields. In the usual surroundings, high value of current radiates strong magnetic field that might exceed the safe limit of creating possible adverse health effects if proper shielding is not ended. Radiated magnetic field at the different locations of engineering workshops are measured and compared with international guidelines. In order to achieve space distribution, the work place is divided into meshes and fields are measured in the grid points. The measurements are performed using three axis EMF meter (Gauss meter). The results and analysis shows that the data taken using the three axis Tesla meter is more accurate with the calculated value compared to the existing single axis Tesla meter.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach to Detect Soft Error
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Error Detecting Codes (EDCs) and Error Correcting Codes (ECCs) stays on top over some of the prevailing soft error mitigating approaches while cost overhead is considered greatly. As soft errors are noteworthy concern for circuit trustworthiness, identification of those will be the key to endure it and furthermore propelling towards recuperation procedure guarantees smooth birch operation through protecting error proliferation. This paper pact with a competent approach by lessen the most important `check-bits' that are to be added up with data to be transmitted. To identify soft errors, the proposed method introduces `self-derived' option for check-bits to be built taking the quantity of minimum existing digit (`0' or `1') in the data word rather than constant consideration (i.e., 1's only). Hence, it reduces the cost as well as memory overhead notably. Moreover, approaching with shortened check-bits have been proved worthy as it is time effective and as the data access rate is low.

articleTitle: A study of Molten carbonate fuel cell based power generation for Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to propose a hybrid power supply system with the existing coal and natural gas based power plant that not only reduce carbon dioxide but also produce power using that CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In this hybrid system a molten carbonate fuel cell (MCFC) is included that captures CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> from existing power plant and through the process of chemical reaction produces dc power. Most of the previous work proposed individual MCFC based power plant or new MCFC based hybrid power plant. Existing power plants of Bangladesh emits CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at a decent rate to be able to cause serious greenhouse effect. But Bangladesh cannot afford to simply stop producing power from the existing power plants just because they are harmful to the environment. Which is why a hybrid power supply system has been proposed here which can make existing power plant environmental friendly while producing power at the same time.

articleTitle: Robust Face Recognition Using Radial Basis Probabilistic Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a human face recognition method based on radial basis probabilistic neural network (RBPNN). Before classification, discrete cosine transform (DCT) is used to extract textural features from frontal face images. Dimension reduction is achieved considering high frequency coefficients as redundant features, thereby omitting them. Subtractive clustering-based RBPNN is used for classification. Two databases - ORL database and LU database are used to evaluate the model. Experimental results demonstrate better classification efficiency of the model with respect to other popular artificial neural networks (ANN) classifiers. Recognition rate of 98% is achieved using this model. 3% and 6% change in recognition rate are observed in ORL and LU database respectively for applying different noise level. Training time remains below 2 sec for both databases.

articleTitle: Stability Improvement of IG Based Wind Farm Using DFIG
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The performance of fixed speed wind turbines is less satisfactory than the modern variable speed wind turbines like Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG). Nowadays DFIGs are playing a significant role in wind turbine industry/wind power generation system due to some of it's special features. To improve the stability of existing fixed speed induction generator (IG) based wind farm different types of controlling strategies are used. In this paper it is seen that DFIG can be used to generate power as well as to increase the stability of an IG based wind farm without any controlling device. This study recommends/suggests to use DFIG for increasing the total capacity of grid connected IG based wind farm. Thus the performance IG can be improved. The simulation analyses have performed using PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Three Different Microstrip Patch Antennas on the Rat Model
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, three different microstrip patch antennas are designed to operate in the ISM band (2.4-2.45 GHz) and their effect on the rat model is analyzed. At first, a rectangular microstrip patch antenna is designed. Then the patch is converted into P-shape and E-shape with an aim to reduce the return loss and see the effects on rat model.
