The Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) based EM simulation software XFdtd is used to determine the electric field distributions which has an impact on the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) value. In this work, the designed antennas are mounted on the rat model and comparison is made among them. Along with the parameters such as return loss, bandwidth, efficiency, the SAR is analyzed. All the three proposed antennas can be used for head-mountable Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) device. The E-shaped antenna gives better results among the three. In the three proposed antenna, Rogers (R03210) material with relative permittivity of 10.2, loss tangent of 0.0027 is used as the substrate with a thickness of 1.58 mm and coaxial feeding is used for the antennas.

articleTitle: Analytical model for coupling Whispering gallery mode silica microcavity for sensing application
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: An analytical expression for the coupling of whispering gallery mode is derived by adding the coupling and intrinsic loss terms. The resonant frequency of a weak probe mode can be shifted by a strong pump mode due to XPM and the frequency shift of the probe is proportional to the pump energy. We found large negative frequency shift when pump and probe power are perfectly matched, consistant with the reported experimental observations. It can also be found that XPM induced frequency shift is much smaller as compared with SPM induced frequency shift due to the lower power coupled to mode 2. This result opens up a range of new applications in nonlinear sensing and quantum optics.

articleTitle: Standard Indices of Power Transmission System Evaluation: Financial and Commercial Point of View
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Economic and reliable operation of power system is a critical foundation to support socio-economic development. Along with technical indicators, financial and commercial indices are also equally important to evaluate the performance of power transmission system. This paper proposed and analyzed a set of financial and commercial indices. Outcome of the Power Grid Company of Bangladesh over last three years were analyzed and presented. With the help of these indices, transmission operators can monitor the trends, take required actions, compare with other utility companies, fix new goals and plan for future development. Ultimately which will help to improve the transmission system performance.

articleTitle: Handling Realtime traffic using congestion control algorithms under Meanfield Domain
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: As the number of internet users is increasing, it causes congestion of TCP/IP network. Since the introduction of multimedia traffic on the internet, it is very challenging to run the multimedia traffic on the internet while TCP traffic is present. The purpose of this paper is to compare and analyze the congestion control and avoidance mechanism which are proposed for the TCP/IP. In this paper, we measure and evaluate the performance of Tahoe, Reno, SACK, and Vegas. It is showed that TCP Vegas measurement of handling congestion is proactive instead of reactive, and Vegas also keep track of segment and able to calculate RTT (Round Trip Time). Results are validated using the simulator and shown that Vegas performance is better as compare to others.

articleTitle: OFDM Time and Frequency Offset Compensated Signal Extraction with Increased SINR for High Detection Probability
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system is multichannel system that provides high rate and high quality wireless communication services, where system performance can be degraded by two factors, one is the symbol timing offset (TOF) and other is the carrier frequency offset (CFO) caused by Doppler frequency shift. After estimating different offsets and compensating them, the detection probability has to be determined whether they are true or false detection. It can be done using Signal to Noise and Interference Ratio (SINR) or estimated received signal power and/or noise power level. This is influenced by the estimated signal retrieving point w.r.t. SINR. In this paper the effect of different kind off offsets are described with the simulated results. A solution for retrieving the estimated signal and calculating the SINR for detection probability has been presented.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PI, PID and Hybrid Fuzzy Controller in Matrix Converter Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The paper depicts a three-phase MC model that has been developed using a well-known method, named Venturini considering the value 0.866 for voltage transfer ratio. Various fluctuations, damping, and mismatches are observed at the converter's output. As voltage transfer ratio possess a great influence on the output frequency, amplitude, and harmonics of MC, it's imperative to control that in order to get the best output of MC. So, firstly in this paper, the conventional PI and PID controllers have been used to control the voltage transfer ratio for the better outcome. However, they have several limitations in case of complex systems. So, an intelligent control method has been commenced named Hybrid Fuzzy (HF) controller which is the combination of PI and FLC. Here, resistive-inductive and induction motor (IM) load are tested with the double of line frequency range of MC. Moreover, an unbalanced grid has been investigated for balancing the magnitude of the three phase voltages. It has been found that HF controller delivers better performance over conventional controllers in each and every task of the MC.

articleTitle: Non Isolated DC-DC Step Up Converter with High Voltage Gain for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In renewable energy applications high step-up dc-dc converters are widely used to maintain an uninterruptible power system. The necessity of a high step-up dc-dc converter is to rise the low voltage from photovoltaic (PV) or fuel cell based grid connected system to a relatively high bus voltage for the downstream dc-ac grid-connected inverter. The voltage gain of the conventional boost converter is restricted due to high ripple current and the low efficiency because of high duty cycle. This paper presents a non-isolated dc-dc step up converter with high voltage gain. The proposed converter can provide a large voltage gain at a small duty ratio. In addition, all the power switches work depending upon a single pulse width modulated (PWM) control signal, reducing the control complexity. At the beginning, the working principle and steady-state analysis in continuous conduction mode are explained in detail. Finally, simulation results justify the analysis of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Servo Controller in Triple-Stage Hard Disk Drive Servo System
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Currently in a hard disk drive (HDD), a voice coil motor (VCM) actuator is used as the primary stage and a piezoelectric actuator is used as the secondary stage of a head positioning control in (x-y) lateral direction. To achieve the future generation high capacity HDDs, the `Thermal Fly-height Control' (TFC) slider is employed as `Thermal Position Control' (TPC) slider. This TPC slider is used as the tertiary stage to control the R/W head in the lateral direction. In this paper, the feasibility of using the TPC slider as a tertiary actuator in a triple-stage HDD is studied through extensive simulation analysis using MATLAB/Simulink. Besides, comparative analysis with dual-stage and single-stage hard disk drive is done. Simulation results substantiate the effectiveness of the triple-stage servo system.

articleTitle: RF Subcarrier Modulated Free Space Communication System with Coherent Optical Receiver under Weak Turbulent Condition
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: To develop a robust communication system in atmospheric turbulent condition subcarrier modulated FSO communication are investigated recently. In this paper an analytical approach is developed to investigate the effect of atmospheric turbulence on BER performance of a RF subcarrier modulated free space optical communication system considering the atmospheric effect under weak turbulent condition which is modeled by lognormal distribution. Analysis is presented to find SNR, BER and power penalty at the output of an optical coherent receiver with a ASK RF subcarrier modulated optical intensity modulator.

articleTitle: Control of Power Factor and Reduction of THD for a Three Phase Grid Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Power electronic converters have the capability to provide both active and reactive power in the multigrid system. If this reactive power supply is not properly controlled, this could lead to a significant degradation of grid power factor and increment in subsequent losses. In this paper, a Park transformation based power factor control algorithm has been developed for a grid connected inverter. To mitigate Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) an even and (nx3) harmonic cancellation based switching system has also been integrated with the control signal. During steady state, the controller has kept the grid Power Factor (PF) to 0.93 and the line voltage THD to 0.094%,0.0834% and 0.0835% for phase A, B, and C respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Communication Satellite at the Proposed Orbital Slots for Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Recently Bangladesh has hired a slot at 119.1° east from Intersputnik International for her maiden communication satellite. Requests for some different slots at 69°, 74°, 102° & 133° East (codenamed as BDSAT-69E, BDSAT-74E, BDSAT-102E, BDSAT-133E) has also been submitted to ITU. Slant height, Elevation, Rain Attenuation & Path Loss for C & Ku band have been analyzed for all of these bands. After the analysis and required calculation, the most appropriate slot for launching satellite for Bangladesh has been chosen. It turned into evident that “102° EAST” is the most suitable slot for Bangladesh. The next suitable slot is “74° EAST”. The performance of the satellite at the other slots have also been analyzed and offered in this paper.

articleTitle: An Improved Graphene FET with Reduced Miller Capacitance Using Extended Gate Structure and Heterogeneous Oxide Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an improved design for graphene field effect transistors (GFETs) to reduce Miller capacitance. We use an in-house built quantum solver of 2D materials to simulate GFET devices. Although gate-drain parasitic Miller capacitance can be reduced with higher drain voltages, it is not a practical solution for devices to be operated over a large drain voltage swing. Therefore, we suggest a novel design in which gate extension near the source region can reduce Miller capacitance significantly. Moreover, it is shown that a heterogeneous oxide dielectric can further reduce Miller capacitance as well as enhance device current. Finally, we present the frequency response of the proposed device to show that it is more suitable for wide bandwidth high frequency applications than the conventional one. Thus, the proposition would be helpful to design low Miller capacitance based high performance FETs with other 2D materials too.

articleTitle: Improved Control of Grid Connected DFIG Wind Turbine Under LVRT Conditions Using Full and Partial Compensation Methods
publicationTitle: 2017 2nd International Conference on Electrical & Electronic Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: For the grid connected doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind turbine, over current flows through the DFIG rotor circuit during grid faults due to stator transient and negative sequence flux. For better control of DFIG, this paper introduces both full and partial series compensation methods that ensures complete safety for the DFIG and also prevents the isolation of DFIG from the grid during grid voltage disturbances. In this method, a cascaded H-bridge 5-level three phase inverter is used which converts the dc voltage from battery energy storage system into three phase ac voltage. The ac voltage is injected in series with the grid through a series injection transformer during grid faults and hence mitigates the effect of voltage sag on the DFIG.
